title: introduce-flashmix-kernel-rotary-offset-tiling-and-continuous-batcher
author: Elena Park
description: Motivation: We see tail latency variance on long-context workloads and suboptimal throughput when small requests mix with long-running KV-heavy traces. This PR introduces a new hybrid attention microkernel ("flashmix") that blends a narrow-window FlashAttention path with a fused rotary precompute stage and a rotary-offset-aware tiling layout. It also wires a scheduler hint and continuous-batcher integration so the runtime dynamically switches tile sizes and KV pinning policies based on observed sequence-length distribution and prefix-hotness. The goals are (1) reduce p95 autoregressive latency for mixed workloads, (2) increase steady-state throughput for long-context reranking/LLM chains, and (3) provide a safe runtime fallback for hardware that cannot run the fused path. Summary of changes: added CUDA microkernel and CPU fallback (src/serving/kernel/flashmix_kernel.cu + .cc), rotary precompute fusion layer that materializes offset anchors to minimize per-step work (src/serving/kernel/rotary_fuse.h), a tiling-aware scheduler that exposes per-request hints and auto-selects tile dimensions (src/serving/scheduler/tiling_scheduler.cpp), KV cache pinning + eviction weight updates (src/serving/cache/kv_pinning.cpp), continuous-batcher adjustments to prefer pooling when many short requests dominate (src/serving/batching/continuous_batcher.cpp), unit and perf tests (tests/attn_flashmix_perf.py, tests/kv_pinning_unit.py), docs and rollout ops (docs/perf/flashmix.md, deploy/rollout/flashmix_flags.md). Backwards compatibility: the feature is behind a runtime flag (--enable-flashmix) and a model capability table entry; when disabled the runtime uses existing FlashAttention or fallback kernels. Rollout plan: Feature flag gated, staged rollout to 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automated perf checks and automatic rollback on >5% quality or >10% latency regression. See ENG-2142 for evaluation prompts and perf harness configs.

release_notes:
- Add new 'flashmix' attention microkernel that fuses small-window FlashAttention with rotary precompute and tiling; disabled by default behind --enable-flashmix flag.
- Tiling scheduler with request-hint API to pick adaptive tile sizes at runtime.
- KV cache pinning policy to keep frequently-accessed prefixes resident and reduce eviction churn.
- Continuous-batcher tuning to prefer pooling for imbalance workloads.
- Performance improvements: p95 latency reductions for mixed short/long workloads and throughput uplift on long-context workloads.
notes_for_oncall: If rollout triggers >10% latency regressions, flip --enable-flashmix=false via the feature flag and the autoscaler will rollback canary; KV pinning changes are additive but may increase memory footprint — watch replica memory and OOM signals.
QA_steps: 1) Build with --enable-flashmix and run tests/attn_flashmix_perf.py against gpuxl-4/5 runners
2) Deploy to staging with 10% traffic and monitor tile-selection metric: runtime.scheduler.tile_selection_distribution
3) Validate model outputs for a representative prompt set (ENG-2142) to ensure no quality regressions
4) If metrics OK, increase rollout to 50% and then 100% with checks after each step
